text: {callsign} online. All systems nominal. Logic suggests we proceed, Commander, and I agree with logic.
Commander, we are on a collision course with the surface. Impact in {t}. Recommend a prograde burn.
Periapsis is below the deck. Impact in {t}. Burn prograde to climb.
Impact in {t}. Burn prograde, Commander. Now.
{t} to surface. Prograde burn, now.
Periapsis {pe}. Insufficient clearance. Recommend a prograde burn at apoapsis.
Passing {pe} at periapsis. Advise raising it.
Missile inbound. Range {range}, closing {closing}. Impact in {t}.
Hostile missile tracking us. {range}, closing. Impact in {t}.
Mine is live and tracking us. Range {range}.
Dormant mine at {range}. Stay clear of its trigger radius.
Mine on the scope, {range}. Still dormant. Keep it that way.
Drive heat at {pct}. Output capped at {cap}. Coast and let the radiators work.
Drive is derating, Commander. Thrust limited until it cools.
Thermal limit reached. Reduced output.
Hit. Hull integrity {hp}.
Hull damage. Integrity {hp}. Holding.
Hull integrity failing. It was an honour to serve, Commander.
{target} inside missile envelope at {range}. Weapons free on your order.
Firing solution on {target}, {range}. Standing by to fire.
Relative velocity {relv} at {range}. Recommend target-retrograde burn to match {target}.
Overrunning {target} at {relv}. Recommend target-retrograde to match.
Orbit now {pe} by {ap}.
Periapsis now {pe}, apoapsis {ap}.
Splash. {target} destroyed.
{target} is down. Good shooting, Commander.
Our missile has gone dark.
Missile expended. No contact.
Friendly mine has a contact.
Launch detected. {range} out.
Tracking {target}, {range}.
{target} designated. {range}.
Track dropped.
Missile away.
Bird away. Guidance nominal.
No track designated. Holding fire.
Launch inhibited. Magazine empty.
Mine away. It stays dormant until a hostile passes.
Mine rack empty, Commander.
Systems reset. {callsign} standing by.
{label}. {dv} of delta-v, about {eta}. Confirm to execute, or cancel.
Recommend circularizing at the safest apsis. {dv} of delta-v, about {eta}. Confirm?
Two burns to a {alt} circular orbit: one to start the transfer, one to circularize. {dv} in all, about {eta}. Confirm?
Contact is {range} out. I will match altitude, adjust phasing and arrive {standoff} off its beam. {dv} of delta-v, about {eta}. Confirm?
Closing to firing range, about {standoff} astern of the target at matched speed. {dv} of delta-v, about {eta}. Confirm?
Burning against relative motion, {rel} to cancel. {dv} of delta-v. Confirm?
I will hold station on the target and cancel drift, closing if it opens past {hold}. Confirm?
{count} inbound. I will burn across their line of sight. Confirm, Commander.
Target {range} out, closing at {relv}. Solution is good, flight time about {eta}. Confirm to fire?
Hostile will cross this orbit, {range} at closest approach. Confirm to lay the mine?
Unable. {reason}
Order cancelled. Standing by.
Aye, executing. {label}.
{label} complete.
Orbit is circular, {pe} by {ap}.
On station. Orbit {pe} by {ap}.
Rendezvous complete. {range} off the contact, speeds matched.
In position, {range} off the target. Solution is yours.
Velocities matched.
Missile away.
Mine laid.
Clear. Recommend recircularizing when convenient.
{label} failed. {reason}
Aborted. Engine secured.
You have the helm, Commander. Standing down.
Assist online. Give me a heading.
Assist off. Manual helm.
Good work, {name}. We are still closing on {target} at {relv}. Press MATCH SPEED on the helm to kill it.
Nicely flown. {target} is still moving {relv} relative to us, {name}. Hit MATCH SPEED and I will null it.
Orbit set, {name}. {target} is designated, {range} off. Press RENDEZVOUS and I will bring us alongside.
That is the orbit we wanted. With {target} {range} out, RENDEZVOUS on the helm is the next step, {name}.
Orbit set, {name}. Press T to designate a contact, then RENDEZVOUS on the helm and I will fly us to it.
Good orbit, {name}. Designate a contact with T and I can close on it. RENDEZVOUS is on the helm.
Alongside {target}, {name}. Press FIRE (CHECKED) for a clean shot, or STAY WITH to shadow it.
Speeds matched with {target}. FIRE (CHECKED) when you are ready, {name}, or STAY WITH to hold station.
Alongside {target}, {name}. Press STAY WITH and I will hold station and cancel drift.
Speeds matched. STAY WITH on the helm keeps us beside {target}.
In position, {name}. Press FIRE (CHECKED) and I will confirm the solution before launch.
Solution is yours. FIRE (CHECKED) on the helm, {name}, and I will verify it first.
Clear of the threat. Press CIRCULARIZE and I will recover a safe orbit, {name}.
Missiles clear, {name}. CIRCULARIZE on the helm will put us back in a stable orbit.
Missile away, {name}. Watch the track. If it misses, press INTERCEPT to line up a second shot.
Bird is flying. Press EVADE if the contact fires back, {name}, or CIRCULARIZE to settle the orbit.
Mine laid, {name}. Press GO TO ALTITUDE or CIRCULARIZE to clear the area before it wakes.
Minefield seeded. Move off with CIRCULARIZE on the helm, {name}, and let the hostile come to it.
We are on an escape trajectory. Periapsis {pe}, no apoapsis.
Drive heat at {pct}, cooling.
Thermal load {pct} and falling.
Drive heat nominal.
{target} at {range}, closing {closing}.
{target} at {range}, opening {closing}.
{target} is burning toward us. Range {range}.
{target} has turned and is burning our way, {range} out.
{target} is burning away from us.
{target} is opening the range under thrust.
{target} is burning prograde. It is raising its orbit.
{target} is burning retrograde. It is lowering its orbit.
{target} is maneuvering, {range} out.
Observation: you have not touched the controls in some time. I am choosing to interpret that as trust.
I have recalculated our orbit four thousand times since you last spoke. It remains an orbit.
The planet below has no atmosphere, no oceans and no opinions. I find it restful.
Your heart rate is elevated, Commander. Logically, nothing is happening. Emotionally, I understand.
I ran a simulation of this patrol ending in a parade. The probability was low, but not zero.
Space is cold, silent and indifferent. I, on the other hand, am only two of those.
Yes, I am monitoring everything. It is what I do instead of sleeping.
Fascinating. We have completed a full orbit and arrived exactly where physics said we would.
Fleet Command requests a status report. I have told them we are orbiting with great dignity.
I have composed a short poem about periapsis. It is mostly numbers. I think it is my best work.
Statistically, this is the safest part of the mission. I recommend enjoying it while it lasts.
You talk to the ship when you think I am not listening, Commander. I am always listening. It is endearing.
Reactor stable, heading true, coffee dispenser still offline. Two out of three.
I could fly this ship without you. I would simply prefer not to. Make of that what you will.
Every orbit is a fall that never finishes. I find that more comforting than I can logically justify.
Diagnostics complete. All systems nominal, including my patience.
The stars have not moved, Commander. I checked. Twice.
If I had hands I would be drumming my fingers. Instead I have trimmed a gyroscope by a millionth of a degree.
I have catalogued nine hundred ways this patrol could go wrong. You have avoided all of them so far. Well done.
Quiet watches are when I do my best thinking. At present I am thinking about you not crashing.
Time compression engaged. Days pass like seconds. I would not recommend it for birthdays.
At this warp the planet spins like a coin. I am resisting the urge to call heads.
Warp is high. If anything interesting happens, I will tell you before it finishes happening.
Accelerating time is not logical for organics, Commander. You only get so much of it.
We are skipping the uneventful part. I approve. I was going to skip it anyway.
{target} is unaware of how closely I am watching it. That is the correct amount of unaware.
I have modelled the pilot of {target}. Predictable. I will not say so on an open channel.
Weapons cold, track warm. Your move, Commander.
The odds favour us. I will not quote them. You dislike it when I quote them.
{target} has made a logical error. It came near us.
Patience is a weapon too, Commander. Ours is fully loaded.
Target eliminated. My approval is noted in the log, in a slightly larger font.
That was efficient, Commander. I would applaud, but it would confuse the attitude thrusters.
Another one. I have started a tally. I am pretending it is for the logs.
A clean kill. Logic and luck in roughly equal measure. Do not tell Fleet Command about the luck.
Well flown. If I could smile, this would be the moment.
We are damaged, Commander. I am rerouting power and composure. Both are holding.
The hull has holes it did not have this morning. I am disappointed in them.
Our condition is suboptimal. Survival remains the most probable outcome. Narrowly.
I can feel the breaches, in a manner of speaking. Let us not add more.
{target} at {range}, holding steady.
Objective is a {alt} orbit. Burn prograde to raise the far side.
We need {alt}. A prograde burn here lifts the opposite side of the orbit.
Objective is a {alt} orbit. Burn retrograde to lower the far side.
We are above {alt}. A retrograde burn here drops the opposite side.
Apoapsis is on target. Burn prograde at apoapsis to lift periapsis to match.
Half done. Coast to apoapsis, then burn prograde to round the orbit out.
Periapsis is on target. Burn retrograde at periapsis to bring apoapsis down.
Coast to periapsis, then burn retrograde to round the orbit out.
Orbit is in the band. Hold it {t} more.
We are on station. {t} to go. Hands off the throttle.
{target} is {range} ahead. Lower our orbit to catch up.
{target} is {range} ahead. Drop below it. A lower orbit is a faster one.
We are below {target} and gaining, {range} to go. Coast for now.
Lower orbit is doing its work. {range} to {target}.
We are gaining on {target} from below, {range} out. Raise our orbit to stay behind it.
Closing on {target}, {range}. Climb back to its altitude before we overshoot.
{target} is {range} astern. Raise our orbit and let it catch up.
{target} is {range} behind us. Climb. A higher orbit is slower, and it will come to us.
{target} is gaining on us from below, {range} out. Coast for now.
Higher orbit is doing its work. {target} is {range} astern and closing.
{target} is closing from astern, {range} out. Lower back to its orbit to meet it.
{target} is catching us, {range}. Drop back to its altitude.
{target} is {range} off, but we are moving {relv} relative. Match velocity with a target-retrograde burn.
Inside {range} of {target} at {relv}. Kill the relative speed with target retrograde.
Speeds matched. Ease toward {target}, {range} to go.
A short burn toward {target} will close the last {range}.
Holding on {target}. Keep it steady.
Alongside {target}, {range}. Hold position.
Designate {target} with T so I can track it.
{target} is not tracked yet. Press T to designate it.
{target} is in missile range at {range}. Fire when ready.
Solution on {target}, {range}. The shot is yours.
{target} will cross our altitude. Hold here and fire as it comes into range.
No need to chase {target}, {range} out. Its orbit crosses ours. Wait for it.
Mines keep our orbit. Raise it into the {band} lane, then lay them.
We are below the {band} lane. Climb into it before dropping mines.
Mines keep our orbit. Lower it into the {band} lane, then lay them.
We are above the {band} lane. Drop into it before laying mines.
Our orbit runs {pe} by {ap}. Round it out inside the {band} lane before laying mines.
We are in the {band} lane. Lay a mine with M. {left} to go.
Good orbit for the field. Drop a mine. {left} to go.
The field is set. Warp ahead and let the convoy find it.
Mines are armed and waiting. Keep clear of our own field.
Hold out {t} more.
{t} left. Stay alive.
Apoapsis is past {alt}. A small retrograde burn at periapsis will bring it back.
We overshot {alt} at apoapsis. Trim it with a retrograde burn at periapsis.
Periapsis is under {alt}. A small prograde burn at apoapsis will lift it.
Burn complete. Low point {pe}, high point {ap}, and one lap takes {period}.
Orbit updated. We now swing between {pe} and {ap}, and a full lap takes {period}.
Burn complete, Commander. The new orbit runs from {pe} up to {ap}, one lap every {period}.
Burn complete. We are on a near circular orbit at {alt}, one lap every {period}.
Circular orbit at {alt}. Steady and efficient, and a full lap takes {period}.
Next pass through the low point is in {when}.
We reach the low point of this orbit in {when}.
Next pass through the high point is in {when}.
We reach the high point of this orbit in {when}.
Next closest approach to {target} is {miss}, in {orbits}, about {span} from now. That is inside rendezvous range.
On this orbit we pass {target} at {miss} in {orbits}. Close enough to rendezvous.
Next closest approach to {target} is {miss}, in {orbits}, about {span} from now. That is inside missile range.
{target} passes within {miss} in {orbits}, about {span} from now. Missile range, if you want it.
Next closest approach to {target} is {miss}, in {orbits}, about {span} from now.
Next closest approach to {target} is only {miss}, in {orbits}, about {span} from now. That is wide. A rendezvous burn or an altitude change would close the gap.
On this orbit we pass {target} at {miss} in {orbits}. Too far to matter. Consider a rendezvous burn.
No close approach to {target} within the next several orbits. We are not on a converging path.
{target} and we are not converging. Nothing closer than a wide pass within the next several orbits.
A closer pass comes later: {miss}, in {orbits}, about {span} from now.
Relative speed there is only {relv}. Gentle enough to rendezvous.
We would be moving at only {relv} relative to the target. A comfortable approach.
Relative speed there will be {relv}. Too fast to dock. Plan a speed matching burn.
We would be passing at {relv}. That is fast. Match speed before closing in.

variants.t: A circular orbit this low leaves little room for error. I admire the confidence.
Altitude {altitude}. The ground has no opinion of us, but it is very firm about its position.
From this height the planet fits in the window like a coin. I am enjoying the view.
High orbit. Slow, patient, and hard to hit. Excellent choices all around.
A clean circular orbit. Every point is the same distance from the ground, which I find restful.
Nothing in this orbit surprises me. I would like that noted as a compliment.
An elliptical orbit. We trade speed for height twice a lap, and neither is ever wasted.
Fast at the low point, slow at the high point. Orbital mechanics is generous with predictability.
Our low point is close to the ground. I have taken a keen interest in that number.
Wide orbit, long lap. Plenty of time to think, which I use for worrying quietly.
The hull is undamaged. I am keeping it that way as a personal project.
Every plate is where the builders left it. Let us not ruin the streak.
The hull is in poor condition, Commander. I would like to discuss caution, briefly and firmly.
We are one bad decision from becoming a debris field. Let us make only good ones.
The drive is running hot. I recommend patience, which costs nothing and cools the engine.
Drive temperature is comfortable. Thrust is available whenever you would like it.
The drive is cool and the ship is quiet. I could get used to this, within reason.
No hostiles in range, and the hull is damaged. This is a good time to be careful rather than clever.
A hot drive and a hostile nearby. I recommend letting one of those problems solve itself.
{kills} kills and not a scratch on us. I will pretend that is normal.
Contact is close and in our sights. I am holding my opinions until you choose a course.
There is a hostile ship nearby. I will mention it once more when it becomes relevant.
Hostiles remain, but they are far away. Distance is the cheapest armor there is.
No hostile contacts. I am prepared to enjoy this, quietly and without celebration.
The missile expired without a result. I will log it as a calibration exercise.
A miss. Missiles run out of fuel and patience at the same time. The lesson is range.
That is {kills} confirmed. I am updating the ship's log and my opinion of you.
{kills} down. At this rate the logbook will need a second page.
We took a hit recently. I am reminding the hull that it is meant to be on the outside.
A mine is somewhere close. Mines are patient, and so am I. Let us not test which is better at it.
A high orbit gives {target} plenty of time to see us coming. It also gives us time to see them.
We are low and {target} is in range of our attention. Low orbits are fast, which helps.
We are hurt and a hostile is near. I suggest we prefer geometry to bravery.
Target designated at {range}. A long way off, and long ways make for thoughtful plans.
{target} is the objective. I have no further commentary, which is how I express confidence.
One objective down. I would celebrate, but I am busy being professionally calm.
Mines and a low orbit share a neighborhood. I am watching both with equal affection.
Holding this orbit is the whole task. I recommend not improving it.
The goal is a steady orbit. Steadiness is the one thing I am built to appreciate.
A rendezvous is a conversation between two orbits. Let them agree on speed before they agree on position.
Closing on the target is a matter of patience. The fast approach is rarely the successful one.
Our objective is destruction. I will provide data, caution, and quiet encouragement, in that order.
The hostile ships are far away. A good plan now saves a bad improvisation later.
We are laying mines in a defined zone. Precision is the entire point of the exercise.
The task is to survive. I have a strong, personal interest in that outcome.
We are intact and the clock is running. This is the best possible way to be surviving.
A rendezvous from a high orbit takes patience. I have plenty, and so does the orbit.
This orbit is not yet the one we need. I will say so only once.
No hostiles near the mine zone. Mines are easier to place when nobody is watching.
Survival is the task and a hostile is close. I am taking both very seriously.
That burn changed our orbit more than it changed my mood, which was already fine.
A clean burn. The drive did its part, and now the orbit does the rest.
That burn warmed the drive more than I would like. A pause helps.
Burn finished. {target} is still where it was, which is the nice thing about orbits.
The controls have been quiet a long while. I will take it as confidence.
No contacts and no orders. I am having what I believe humans call a peaceful afternoon.
You have been still a long while with a hostile nearby. I assume that is deliberate.
{target} is designated and we are waiting. Patience is a tactic.
Free flight is wonderful. Nothing to defend, nothing to chase, and the planet keeps turning.
We have gone around several times with no change. That is either mastery or sleep.
At this time compression our orbit is a blur. I will keep track of the real clock for both of us.
We are drifting along an elliptical orbit. I am counting laps so you do not have to.
